title: Who May Come Near God
overview: In Ezekiel's vision of a restored temple, God sets rules about who may enter, who may serve as priests, and how those priests must live.

parts.label: The shut east gate (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: God's glory entered the temple through the east gate in the previous chapter, so that gate now stays shut forever as a mark of honor. Only the prince, the leader of the restored people, may sit inside it to eat a sacred meal before the LORD, though scholars are unsure exactly who this figure is meant to be.

parts.label: Outsiders kept out (vv. 4-9)
parts.note: Ezekiel again sees God's glory fill the temple and hears that Israel had let outsiders handle holy duties instead of doing the work themselves. These outsiders had neither circumcision, the outward sign of belonging to God's covenant (binding agreement) with Israel, nor any inner commitment to it, and they are now barred from the sanctuary.

parts.label: Levites lose their rank (vv. 10-14)
parts.note: Levites, the tribe set apart for temple work, who had led worship before idols may no longer serve as priests at the altar. They keep lower jobs such as guarding gates and slaughtering animals for the people, and many scholars link this to the closing of local shrines earlier in Judah's history.

parts.label: Zadok's line as priests (vv. 15-16)
parts.note: Zadok was chief priest under King David and King Solomon, and his descendants are described as having stayed loyal when others turned away. They alone may approach the altar and God's table to offer sacrifices.

parts.label: How priests must live (vv. 17-27)
parts.note: Priests wear cool linen rather than sweaty wool, change clothes before meeting the people because holiness was thought to pass by touch, and follow rules on hair, wine, marriage and contact with the dead. Their job is also to teach the difference between holy and ordinary, clean and unclean, and to settle disputes by God's laws.

parts.label: How priests are supported (vv. 28-31)
parts.note: Priests own no land, because God himself is their inheritance, meaning they live from what people give to God. The people give them portions of offerings and the first of their harvests and dough, and priests may not eat animals found dead or killed by wild beasts.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether Ezekiel's temple describes a literal future temple with real priests and sacrifices or is a symbolic picture of God dwelling with his people, which many read as fulfilled in Jesus and the church.
think: When someone has failed in a position of trust, what would a fair response look like: removal, a lesser role, or a full second chance?
